message.reasoning:
I'm planning JUnit 4 test cases for jsoup's Cleaner class, covering constructor null-whitelist exceptions, clean() behavior with null and valid documents, isValid() true/false branches, and the copySafeNodes path.

Writing Cleaner test cases...

Adding more test cases...

I'm verifying the comment is stripped while visible text remains, then setting up another test where a disallowed tag like span wraps an allowed tag like b to check recursion into unsafe elements.

I'm also adding a test confirming that unsafe attributes like onclick get discarded while safe ones like href are preserved after cleaning with the basic whitelist.

Then I'm checking that the enforced attribute behavior works correctly—verifying rel="nofollow" gets automatically added to anchor tags since Whitelist.basic() enforces that attribute. After that I'm starting a new section for isValid() tests, beginning with a check that it throws when given a null document.

Now I'm adding tests for isValid() returning true when all content passes the whitelist cleanly, false when an unsafe tag like script gets discarded, and false when an unsafe attribute like onclick gets stripped from an otherwise valid element.

I also need to confirm Validate.notNull is from org.jsoup.helper and check that Whitelist.basic() enforces the "nofollow" rel attribute on anchor tags, matching jsoup's source behavior.

For Whitelist.none(), no tags are considered safe at all, and for an empty HTML string there should be nothing discarded since no elements exist to flag.

Now I'm checking whether "span" belongs to Whitelist.basic()'s safe tag list, since cleanRecursesIntoUnsafeTagWithSafeChildren depends on that - looking at jsoup's source list of allowed tags like "a", "b", "blockquote", "br", "cite".

Confirmed: span isn't part of basic's tag set, matching the test expectation. Next I'm verifying cleanIgnoresComments with Whitelist.relaxed() - comments aren't Element or TextNode instances, so they're skipped by the cleaner entirely, which lines up with what the source does. Now moving to constructorThrowsOnNullW test.

I'll check what exception Validate.notNull throws - likely IllegalArgumentException, though I'll lean on the generic Exception class to be safe since I'm not fully certain of the exact behavior, and I'll note that uncertainty in a comment per the requirements. Then I'll put together the summary table, making sure every test aligns with actual jsoup behavior around the version I'm referencing.

I need to be careful with cleanDiscardsUnsafeAttributes - jsoup's default parser won't flag "onclick" as XSS during parsing, it'll just store it as a normal attribute, but Whitelist.basic().isSafeAttribute("a", el, attr) should filter it out since only "href" and "title" are in the allowed attributes list for the "a" tag based on the jsoup Whitelist source.

This checks out, so I'll write a summary table.
